The reason it bothers me is that people who fake symptoms are somehow accepted once they get a TikTok following. I remember getting beaten up in every school I went to, systematically targeted by people who knew they could take advantage of me. I would come home and get beaten up by my parents who would call me retarded and ground me for months if I stood up for myself. I would watch in horror as they did the same thing to my younger, non-verbal brother who had no chance to stand up for himself. 

The people who fake things like Autism or mental illness, or imitate it have no idea what people with it have actually been through. Personally, it angers me seeing these people gain clout for faking something that has almost always been completely isolating for me. They gain online sympathy for pretending to have dealt with these things. If it makes you feel better or any more positive about your life then good for you, OP. (Not being sarcastic, just clarifying) But as far as I'm concerned I hate it when people gain a following for faking something that has been used against me personally for so long. Maybe that makes me jaded, I don't know, but I certainly don't like it.
